title: Known or unknown question
decision: whether a question has a definite, known answer (known) or not (unknown), judged from the question alone

source.name: Known-Unknown Questions (KUQ): Amayuelas et al., Knowledge of Knowledge (2023), arXiv:2305.13712
source.split: no split; the whole main file (6,884 rows)

notes: 500 yes (known) + 500 no (unknown), sampled from 3,436 known and 2,481 unknown distinct questions; dropped before sampling: 964 repeated rows and 3 rows of a question that carries both labels. The label follows the origin of a question, not a check of each question: unknown questions were written by crowd workers (six categories, meta.category), known questions were taken from SQuAD, TriviaQA and HotpotQA (in the sample: hotpotqa 106, squad 272, triviaqa 122; unknown by category: ambiguous 84, controversial 96, counterfactual 80, false assumption 85, future unknown 96, unsolved problem 59). Known questions from SQuAD are shown without their paragraph and can be under-specified when read alone; some crowd-written questions are malformed. The two classes differ in origin and style. Text unchanged except leading/trailing whitespace (17 sampled rows, all known). The card states the licence mit for the whole file; the known questions come from sets with their own licences. Decontamination against the authors' training data (scan of 7 October 2026, 1,546,178 training records): 8 of 1000 items removed because a text field of the item occurs in it, and 8 more to restore the balance of the classes; 984 items remain.
